Co-authors: @jychen21 @AichenF
Submitted by: @GnohzZ 

> **Dependency scope:** this is opt-in, experimental SM120 support requiring a FlashInfer build containing flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6346 (validated at source revision `399b6c1d31a13f38dd827018f89c6a04c8487acb`). The FlashInfer `0.7.2` pin and Docker/CI dependencies are unchanged; `0.7.2` does not contain #6346, so selecting SM120 MegaMoE with it gives an explicit startup error, and the regular SM120 backend remains available. Out-of-box support will follow a FlashInfer release that includes #6346. Rebased onto main `fd5c52588f`.

## Motivation

`--moe-a2a-backend flashinfer_megamoe` currently requires SM100. FlashInfer #6346 added `sm120_mxfp4_mxfp8_bf16_cake`, a fused EP all-to-all + MXFP4 x MXFP8 expert-compute kernel for SM120 (RTX PRO Blackwell) that runs through the same `flashinfer.moe_ep.MoEEpMegaLayer` API this backend already uses. This PR wires it into the existing `flashinfer_megamoe` path for FP4-expert checkpoints, starting with DeepSeek-V4-Flash.

The kernel targets **prefill**. On 4x RTX PRO 5000 Blackwell (72 GB, PCIe) it roughly doubles prefill throughput over `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4` at the same TP4 / attention-DP4 layout, while decode with a few requests per rank is slower (numbers below). The recommended use is the prefill server of a PD-disaggregated deployment, with decode on the existing SM120 recipe; the server logs this at startup when it is not a PD prefill server.

## Modifications

1. **SM120 branch of `flashinfer_megamoe`** (`layers/moe/flashinfer_megamoe.py`, `arg_groups/moe_hook.py`, `environ.py`); SM100 code paths are unchanged:
   - Platform gate: SM120 with compute capability exactly 12.0, FP4 experts, EP >= 2, and a FlashInfer build exporting `Sm120_Mxfp4_Mxfp8_Bf16_Cake_MegaMoeConfig` (clear error otherwise). `--enable-eplb` is rejected (the packed scales are not expert-major); speculative decoding without an explicit `--speculative-moe-runner-backend` is rejected (the default draft runner `flashinfer_trtllm` is SM100-only).
   - `NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1` by default on this path: the kernel joins the EP group's NCCL communicator through NCCL's Device API, which needs cuMem buffers (SGLang otherwise sets it to 0). Same pattern as the `deepep_v2` branch.
   - Weights: FlashInfer's own preprocessing (`preprocess_sm120_mxfp4_mxfp8_cake_mega_weights`). FC1 is a gate/up row interleave of `w13` and is written back into `w13`; FC1/FC2 alias the layer weights, so the experts stay resident once. The float32 (E8M0-widened) checkpoint scales are converted exactly to UE8M0 bytes and replaced by the packed kernel scales.
   - Forward: one workspace per layer; each call stages `compile_tokens_per_rank = max(get_dp_global_num_tokens())`, identical on every EP rank, so there is no per-layer routing all-gather / host sync, and each decode CUDA-graph batch size captures its own bucket. `MegaMoeTunedForward` is not used on SM120 (it would build one compiled kernel + NCCL window set per profiled capacity). Router ids are widened to int64 for this kernel.
   - `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_MEGAMOE_SM120_TRANSPORT_TABLE` (default `lsa_where_reachable`) selects the peer transport; FlashInfer validates the value.
2. **Docs**: DeepSeek-V4 cookbook, new "FlashInfer MegaMoE on SM120 for prefill (Experimental)" note.

Earlier revisions of this PR also changed `deepseek_v2.py` (expert-id remapping under static placement) and `deepseek_v4.py` (MoE output finalization for `flashinfer_megamoe`); upstream #44994 and #46365 now cover both, so they were dropped and this PR touches no model code or tests.

**Validation of the current revision** (on main `fd5c52588f`, 2026-10-26): pre-commit passed for all changed files; existing CPU suites (V4 boundary, layer boundary, FlashInfer MegaMoE, server args, model overrides, runtime context, MXFP8 runner backend): 1045 passed, 1 skipped. GPU on 4x RTX PRO 5000 Blackwell (TP4 / attention-DP4, FlashInfer source `399b6c1d` plus main's new dependency pins, decode CUDA graphs on), GSM8K-200 (`run_eval`, 5-shot) after a 4-prompt smoke, 0 errors in server logs:

| config | GSM8K-200 |
|---|---|
| `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4` (baseline) | 0.985 |
| `--moe-a2a-backend flashinfer_megamoe` (this PR) | 0.990 |
| this PR + `--init-expert-location <recording> --ep-num-redundant-experts 32 --ep-dispatch-algorithm static` | 0.980 |

SM100 was not re-tested (no hardware here); this PR does not change the SM100 code paths.

**Earlier measurements.** The accuracy, speed and topology results below were collected on an earlier revision of this PR; the SM120 runtime code (weight preprocessing, forward, kernel config) is unchanged since, and later revisions only removed startup checks, tests and model-code changes now covered upstream. Environment: one host, 8x NVIDIA RTX PRO 5000 Blackwell 72 GB (SM120, PCIe, two CPU sockets), driver 580.95.05; image `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-cu13` built 2026-10-13 (CUDA 13.0, torch 2.14.1+cu130, NCCL 2.30.7, nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.8.0) with this branch on top of `27b68303d0` and FlashInfer main `399b6c1d` (#6346) from source; model `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`; sgl-eval 0.1.2. Unless noted: `--tp 4 --attn-dp-size 4` on GPUs 0-3.

## Accuracy Tests

DeepSeek-V4-Flash (0731), 4x RTX PRO 5000 Blackwell 72 GB (PCIe), `--tp 4 --attn-dp-size 4`.

**GSM8K-1319** (`sgl-eval run gsm8k --load-preset-from-model-id deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`, sgl-eval 0.1.2: the model's preset, thinking on, temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, max_tokens 200000, reasoning_effort=max):

| config | score | truncated | error |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4` (baseline) | 96.59 % | 0 % | 0 % |
| `--moe-a2a-backend flashinfer_megamoe` (this PR) | 96.13 % | 0 % | 0 % |

**GPQA-diamond** (`sgl-eval run gpqa --from-dataset <gpqa_diamond.jsonl> --load-preset-from-model-id deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 --n-repeats 4`, sgl-eval 0.1.2, 198 questions x 4 repeats). Both arms used the model preset: temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, max_tokens 200000, reasoning_effort=max, and `chat_template_kwargs={"thinking": true}`.

| config | pass@1 (avg of 4) | repeat-level SEM | pass@4 | majority@4 | truncated | error |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `flashinfer_mxfp4` | 90.28 % | 0.56 % | 93.94 % | 90.15 % | 0.00 % | 0.00 % |
| `flashinfer_megamoe` | 90.15 % | 0.44 % | 93.94 % | 90.66 % | 0.00 % | 0.00 % |

These results replace the earlier temperature-0 / 32k-cap run. Scores were independently recomputed from all 792 outputs per arm. The SEM is across four repeats of the same 198 questions; it is not a confidence interval over independently sampled questions or a formal equivalence test.

**AIME25** (the fixture shared with the DeepSeek-V4 cookbook tests in `test/manual/dsv4/`, run locally with the cookbook recipe: sgl-eval, 30 x 16 repeats, thinking on, temperature 1.0, top-p 1.0, `--max-tokens 65536`): pass@1 = 98.1 % (SEM 0.5 %), pass@16 = 100 %, no truncation, threshold 0.93. The GSM8K smoke of the same fixture passes as well.

**Static EPLB** (a recording of V4-Flash routing, `--init-expert-location <file> --ep-dispatch-algorithm static`, no `--enable-eplb`) on this PR's backend (earlier revision, which carried a remap fix now covered upstream by #44994); GSM8K-200 via the deprecated `sglang.test.run_eval` (5-shot), run before upstream moved to sgl-eval:

| config | GSM8K-200 | pf1k input tok/s | ShareGPT input tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|
| this PR, no EPLB | 0.990 | 26109 | 1561 |
| this PR, recorded placement, 0 redundant experts | 0.990 | 25013 | 1507 |
| this PR, recorded placement, 32 redundant experts | 0.990 | 25633 | 1453 |

(The no-EPLB reference is the median of three rounds; the recorded-placement rows are single rounds. They demonstrate functional correctness, not a controlled estimate of remapping overhead.) On the current revision, where the remap comes from upstream #44994, the 32-redundant-expert configuration gives GSM8K-200 = 0.980 (validation table above).

**PD-disaggregated functional check** (cake prefill server on GPUs 0-3 with `--disaggregation-mode prefill`, `flashinfer_mxfp4` decode server on GPUs 4-7, NIXL/UCX KV transfer over RoCE, `sglang_router --pd-disaggregation`): coherent smoke answers and GSM8K-200 = 0.990 (`run_eval`) in two separate runs. (In the second run one request hit the 300 s disaggregation bootstrap timeout before its prefill started.) PD throughput was not measured.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same setup; `--chunked-prefill-size 16384 --max-prefill-tokens 4096` (4096 prefill tokens per rank), `--mem-fraction-static 0.8`, decode CUDA graphs on (prefill CUDA graphs are disabled for DeepSeek-V4 by SGLang's own rule), `sglang.benchmark.serving --dataset-name random-ids`. Prefill: a dedicated rerun on 2026-10-15 with radix cache disabled, three rounds per point, all three backends on the same production tree. Decode: the earlier c7 session on the same production tree, one round per point; GSM8K-200 (sgl-eval preset) in that session: 96.5 % / 97.0 % / 97.0 %.

**Prefill** (OSL 1, `--max-concurrency 64`, `--disable-radix-cache`), input tokens/s (TTFT mean / median / P99, ms). Both baselines run W4A8 (MXFP4 weights x MXFP8 activations, FlashInfer CUTLASS fused MoE) with the tokens all-gathered over attention DP and reduce-scattered after the MoE; `--ep-size 4` places whole experts per rank like this PR:

| ISL | flashinfer_mxfp4, TP MoE | flashinfer_mxfp4, EP4 | flashinfer_megamoe | vs TP / vs EP4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 512 | 12125 (2669 / 2630 / 3670) | 13853 (2334 / 2279 / 3243) | 24174 (1336 / 1291 / 1982) | 1.99x / 1.75x |
| 1024 | 12332 (5126 / 5289 / 6301) | 14165 (4462 / 4603 / 5483) | 25106 (2518 / 2583 / 3121) | 2.04x / 1.77x |
| 2048 | 12101 (9861 / 10774 / 11961) | 13854 (8611 / 9411 / 10469) | 24085 (4950 / 5367 / 6086) | 1.99x / 1.74x |
| 4096 | 11935 (17502 / 21537 / 23239) | 13644 (15287 / 18821 / 20285) | 23400 (8923 / 10887 / 11918) | 1.96x / 1.72x |

In this serving configuration, EP4 improves the baseline by about 1.14-1.15x and the MegaMoE backend is 1.72-1.77x faster than that EP4 baseline (1.96-2.04x over TP MoE). This comparison measures the complete backend, including communication and integration; it does not isolate kernel fusion alone.

Each prefill round has 524288 requested input tokens (`num-prompts = 524288 / ISL`), request rate infinity, concurrency 64, temperature 0, and client seeds 101, 102 and 103; a separate cold run is excluded. The server uses `--disable-radix-cache` and each benchmark passes `--flush-cache`. All 36 measured runs completed every request without errors; all output lengths are one token. The table reports medians of three run-level metrics (including run-level P99s), not pooled request percentiles. The largest per-point throughput range `(max-min)/median` across the three rounds was 0.8% / 0.6% / 3.1% for TP / EP4 / MegaMoE respectively. The runs were sequential on one host, so these are synthetic serving measurements, not a PD throughput or kernel microbenchmark result.

Decode uses seed 42, concurrency 4/16/64/256 and 32/32/128/512 requests respectively; all measured output lengths are 1024 tokens. These earlier decode runs retained radix caching and did not explicitly flush between cases.

**Decode** (ISL 128 / OSL 1024, ignore_eos), median TPOT (ms):

| concurrency (req/rank) | flashinfer_mxfp4, TP MoE | flashinfer_mxfp4, `--ep-size 4` | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 (1) | 15.4 | 16.0 | 21.6 |
| 16 (4) | 21.0 | 22.0 | 27.1 |
| 64 (16) | 33.4 | 33.4 | 37.0 |
| 256 (64) | 61.7 | 60.9 | 60.2 |

Hence the prefill positioning. Decode CUDA graphs capture one bucket per batch size: with `--disable-cuda-graph` the median TPOT of this PR is 65.1 / 62.6 / 62.9 ms at concurrency 4 / 16 / 64 (mxfp4: 66.3 / 65.4 / 66.6 ms).

**Topology (supplementary, historical cache-enabled runs).** The kernel picks a per-peer transport: NCCL LSA (CUDA peer access over PCIe/NVLink) where peers can reach each other and NCCL GIN (GPU-initiated RDMA over the NIC) elsewhere. `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_MEGAMOE_SM120_TRANSPORT_TABLE` selects the table. Prefill, OSL 1, `--max-concurrency 128`, input tokens/s for ISL 2048 / 4096:

| cake layout | GPUs | flashinfer_mxfp4 (TP MoE, EP=1) | this PR, `lsa_where_reachable` (default) | this PR, `all_gin` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TP4 / attn-DP4 / EP4 | 0-3, one CPU socket | 12126 / 12130 | 24283 / 23629 (2.00x / 1.95x) | 24563 / 23967 (2.03x / 1.98x) |
| TP8 / attn-DP8 / EP8 | 0-7, two CPU sockets | 13578 / 14855 | 40690 / 42221 (3.00x / 2.84x) | 41629 / 44673 (3.07x / 3.01x) |

At EP8 the two sockets have no CUDA peer path between them, so the default table runs LSA for the 24 directed off-diagonal peer pairs inside the sockets and GIN for the 32 directed pairs across sockets (56 off-diagonal pairs in total); an all-LSA table is not possible on this host. At EP8 this PR needed `--mem-fraction-static 0.70` on these 72 GB GPUs (at 0.80 the first MegaMoE launch ran out of memory); the EP8 rows of both backends use 0.70. GSM8K-200 (`run_eval`) was 0.985-0.990 in every layout.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

nodes.body:
@Fridge003 Thanks, rebased and resolved the conflicts.

The branch is now based on main (16eb87c); the conflict with #44036 (W4A16/SiTU) in flashinfer_megamoe.py has been resolved.

While re-validating on GPU, I hit a regression from #43607: the V4 decoder unconditionally passes leave_output_sum=True, but flashinfer_megamoe completes the EP combine inside its kernel and its FFN transport declares no sum group. The normal MoE path therefore returns MoEOutput pieces that the transport rejects during warmup with “transport finalize owes an undeclared sum group”.

The fix (bda748bc06) disables leave_output_sum specifically for flashinfer_megamoe, preserving other backends’ existing behavior. Tests exercise the real decoder and transport finalization, including a DeepGEMM fallback control. That fallback has a separate unresolved reduction-ownership issue and is not fixed here. The FlashInfer regression likely affects SM100 too; I could only verify it on SM120.

Btw, FlashInfer 0.7.2 does not include flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6346 yet, so the SM120 path remains an opt-in source install, with an explicit startup error under the default pin.

<!-- mintlify-fork-preview-approval -->
### Preview approval required

This pull request comes from a fork, so Mintlify won't build a preview until someone with write access approves commit `0386d3c`.

[Approve preview](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44359/checks?check_run_id=121442305975)

@Fridge003 Rebased onto main and resolved the conflict. The PR now only touches the SM120 path (`flashinfer_megamoe.py`, `moe_hook.py`, `environ.py`) and the cookbook; the `deepseek_v2.py` / `deepseek_v4.py` changes are dropped since #44994 and #46365 cover them.
Please remove all the changes under test folder, unless it's for fixing
Why changing the logic here? When eplb is not enabled, we shouldn't set a non None value here

| `--moe-a2a-backend flashinfer_megamoe` (this PR) | 0.990 |
| this PR + `--init-expert-location <recording> --ep-num-redundant-experts 32 --ep-dispatch-algorithm static` | 0.980 |

SM100 was not re-tested (no hardware here); this PR does not change the SM100 code paths.

**Earlier measurements.** The accuracy, speed and topology results below were collected on an earlier revision of this PR; the SM120 runtime code (weight preprocessing, forward, kernel config) is unchanged since, and later revisions only removed startup checks, tests and model-code changes now covered upstream. Environment: one host, 8x NVIDIA RTX PRO 5000 Blackwell 72 GB (SM120, PCIe, two CPU sockets), driver 580.95.05; image `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-cu13` built 2026-10-13 (CUDA 13.0, torch 2.14.1+cu130, NCCL 2.30.7, nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.8.0) with this branch on top of `27b68303d0` and FlashInfer main `399b6c1d` (#6346) from source; model `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`; sgl-eval 0.1.2. Unless noted: `--tp 4 --attn-dp-size 4` on GPUs 0-3.

## Accuracy Tests

DeepSeek-V4-Flash (0731), 4x RTX PRO 5000 Blackwell 72 GB (PCIe), `--tp 4 --attn-dp-size 4`.

**GSM8K-1319** (`sgl-eval run gsm8k --load-preset-from-model-id deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`, sgl-eval 0.1.2: the model's preset, thinking on, temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, max_tokens 200000, reasoning_effort=max):

| config | score | truncated | error |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4` (baseline) | 96.59 % | 0 % | 0 % |
| `--moe-a2a-backend flashinfer_megamoe` (this PR) | 96.13 % | 0 % | 0 % |

**GPQA-diamond** (`sgl-eval run gpqa --from-dataset <gpqa_diamond.jsonl> --load-preset-from-model-id deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 --n-repeats 4`, sgl-eval 0.1.2, 198 questions x 4 repeats). Both arms used the model preset: temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, max_tokens 200000, reasoning_effort=max, and `chat_template_kwargs={"thinking": true}`.

| config | pass@1 (avg of 4) | repeat-level SEM | pass@4 | majority@4 | truncated | error |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `flashinfer_mxfp4` | 90.28 % | 0.56 % | 93.94 % | 90.15 % | 0.00 % | 0.00 % |
| `flashinfer_megamoe` | 90.15 % | 0.44 % | 93.94 % | 90.66 % | 0.00 % | 0.00 % |

These results replace the earlier temperature-0 / 32k-cap run. Scores were independently recomputed from all 792 outputs per arm. The SEM is across four repeats of the same 198 questions; it is not a confidence interval over independently sampled questions or a formal equivalence test.

**AIME25** (the fixture shared with the DeepSeek-V4 cookbook tests in `test/manual/dsv4/`, run locally with the cookbook recipe: sgl-eval, 30 x 16 repeats, thinking on, temperature 1.0, top-p 1.0, `--max-tokens 65536`): pass@1 = 98.1 % (SEM 0.5 %), pass@16 = 100 %, no truncation, threshold 0.93. The GSM8K smoke of the same fixture passes as well.

**Static EPLB** (a recording of V4-Flash routing, `--init-expert-location <file> --ep-dispatch-algorithm static`, no `--enable-eplb`) on this PR's backend (earlier revision, which carried a remap fix now covered upstream by #44994); GSM8K-200 via the deprecated `sglang.test.run_eval` (5-shot), run before upstream moved to sgl-eval:

| config | GSM8K-200 | pf1k input tok/s | ShareGPT input tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|
| this PR, no EPLB | 0.990 | 26109 | 1561 |
| this PR, recorded placement, 0 redundant experts | 0.990 | 25013 | 1507 |
| this PR, recorded placement, 32 redundant experts | 0.990 | 25633 | 1453 |

(The no-EPLB reference is the median of three rounds; the recorded-placement rows are single rounds. They demonstrate functional correctness, not a controlled estimate of remapping overhead.) On the current revision, where the remap comes from upstream #44994, the 32-redundant-expert configuration gives GSM8K-200 = 0.980 (validation table above).

**PD-disaggregated functional check** (cake prefill server on GPUs 0-3 with `--disaggregation-mode prefill`, `flashinfer_mxfp4` decode server on GPUs 4-7, NIXL/UCX KV transfer over RoCE, `sglang_router --pd-disaggregation`): coherent smoke answers and GSM8K-200 = 0.990 (`run_eval`) in two separate runs. (In the second run one request hit the 300 s disaggregation bootstrap timeout before its prefill started.) PD throughput was not measured.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same setup; `--chunked-prefill-size 16384 --max-prefill-tokens 4096` (4096 prefill tokens per rank), `--mem-fraction-static 0.8`, decode CUDA graphs on (prefill CUDA graphs are disabled for DeepSeek-V4 by SGLang's own rule), `sglang.benchmark.serving --dataset-name random-ids`. Prefill: a dedicated rerun on 2026-10-15 with radix cache disabled, three rounds per point, all three backends on the same production tree. Decode: the earlier c7 session on the same production tree, one round per point; GSM8K-200 (sgl-eval preset) in that session: 96.5 % / 97.0 % / 97.0 %.

**Prefill** (OSL 1, `--max-concurrency 64`, `--disable-radix-cache`), input tokens/s (TTFT mean / median / P99, ms). Both baselines run W4A8 (MXFP4 weights x MXFP8 activations, FlashInfer CUTLASS fused MoE) with the tokens all-gathered over attention DP and reduce-scattered after the MoE; `--ep-size 4` places whole experts per rank like this PR:

| ISL | flashinfer_mxfp4, TP MoE | flashinfer_mxfp4, EP4 | flashinfer_megamoe | vs TP / vs EP4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 512 | 12125 (2669 / 2630 / 3670) | 13853 (2334 / 2279 / 3243) | 24174 (1336 / 1291 / 1982) | 1.99x / 1.75x |
| 1024 | 12332 (5126 / 5289 / 6301) | 14165 (4462 / 4603 / 5483) | 25106 (2518 / 2583 / 3121) | 2.04x / 1.77x |
| 2048 | 12101 (9861 / 10774 / 11961) | 13854 (8611 / 9411 / 10469) | 24085 (4950 / 5367 / 6086) | 1.99x / 1.74x |
| 4096 | 11935 (17502 / 21537 / 23239) | 13644 (15287 / 18821 / 20285) | 23400 (8923 / 10887 / 11918) | 1.96x / 1.72x |

In this serving configuration, EP4 improves the baseline by about 1.14-1.15x and the MegaMoE backend is 1.72-1.77x faster than that EP4 baseline (1.96-2.04x over TP MoE). This comparison measures the complete backend, including communication and integration; it does not isolate kernel fusion alone.

Each prefill round has 524288 requested input tokens (`num-prompts = 524288 / ISL`), request rate infinity, concurrency 64, temperature 0, and client seeds 101, 102 and 103; a separate cold run is excluded. The server uses `--disable-radix-cache` and each benchmark passes `--flush-cache`. All 36 measured runs completed every request without errors; all output lengths are one token. The table reports medians of three run-level metrics (including run-level P99s), not pooled request percentiles. The largest per-point throughput range `(max-min)/median` across the three rounds was 0.8% / 0.6% / 3.1% for TP / EP4 / MegaMoE respectively. The runs were sequential on one host, so these are synthetic serving measurements, not a PD throughput or kernel microbenchmark result.

Decode uses seed 42, concurrency 4/16/64/256 and 32/32/128/512 requests respectively; all measured output lengths are 1024 tokens. These earlier decode runs retained radix caching and did not explicitly flush between cases.

**Decode** (ISL 128 / OSL 1024, ignore_eos), median TPOT (ms):

| concurrency (req/rank) | flashinfer_mxfp4, TP MoE | flashinfer_mxfp4, `--ep-size 4` | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 (1) | 15.4 | 16.0 | 21.6 |
| 16 (4) | 21.0 | 22.0 | 27.1 |
| 64 (16) | 33.4 | 33.4 | 37.0 |
| 256 (64) | 61.7 | 60.9 | 60.2 |

Hence the prefill positioning. Decode CUDA graphs capture one bucket per batch size: with `--disable-cuda-graph` the median TPOT of this PR is 65.1 / 62.6 / 62.9 ms at concurrency 4 / 16 / 64 (mxfp4: 66.3 / 65.4 / 66.6 ms).

**Topology (supplementary, historical cache-enabled runs).** The kernel picks a per-peer transport: NCCL LSA (CUDA peer access over PCIe/NVLink) where peers can reach each other and NCCL GIN (GPU-initiated RDMA over the NIC) elsewhere. `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_MEGAMOE_SM120_TRANSPORT_TABLE` selects the table. Prefill, OSL 1, `--max-concurrency 128`, input tokens/s for ISL 2048 / 4096:

| cake layout | GPUs | flashinfer_mxfp4 (TP MoE, EP=1) | this PR, `lsa_where_reachable` (default) | this PR, `all_gin` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TP4 / attn-DP4 / EP4 | 0-3, one CPU socket | 12126 / 12130 | 24283 / 23629 (2.00x / 1.95x) | 24563 / 23967 (2.03x / 1.98x) |
| TP8 / attn-DP8 / EP8 | 0-7, two CPU sockets | 13578 / 14855 | 40690 / 42221 (3.00x / 2.84x) | 41629 / 44673 (3.07x / 3.01x) |

At EP8 the two sockets have no CUDA peer path between them, so the default table runs LSA for the 24 directed off-diagonal peer pairs inside the sockets and GIN for the 32 directed pairs across sockets (56 off-diagonal pairs in total); an all-LSA table is not possible on this host. At EP8 this PR needed `--mem-fraction-static 0.70` on these 72 GB GPUs (at 0.80 the first MegaMoE launch ran out of memory); the EP8 rows of both backends use 0.70. GSM8K-200 (`run_eval`) was 0.985-0.990 in every layout.

 token-split scheme, and larger values reserve more HBM.
 
+<a id="sm120-flashinfer-megamoe" />
+
+**FlashInfer MegaMoE on SM120 for prefill (Experimental)**
+
+On SM120 (RTX PRO Blackwell), DeepSeek-V4-Flash (FP4 experts) can run its routed
+experts through FlashInfer's fused EP all-to-all + expert-compute kernel
+(`sm120_mxfp4_mxfp8_bf16_cake`, [flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6346](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/6346)).
+It is meant for **prefill**, e.g. the prefill server of a PD-disaggregated deployment:
+decode batches of a few requests per rank run slower than with
+`--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4`, so serve decode with the regular SM120 recipe.
+
+This backend needs a FlashInfer build that contains #6346. The released FlashInfer
+`0.7.2` does not, and selecting the backend with it fails at startup with an explicit
+error. Until a release includes it, build FlashInfer from source at commit `399b6c1d`
+or later ([installation guide](https://docs.flashinfer.ai/installation.html)).
+
+```bash Command
+sglang serve \
+  --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
+  --trust-remote-code \
+  --tp 4 --attn-dp-size 4 \
+  --moe-a2a-backend flashinfer_megamoe \
+  --chunked-prefill-size 16384 --max-prefill-tokens 4096 \
+  --mem-fraction-static 0.8 \
+  --disaggregation-mode prefill \
+  --disaggregation-transfer-backend nixl
+```
+
+- `--max-prefill-tokens` (per rank) sizes the kernel's per-rank workspace; larger
+  values reserve more memory. `--chunked-prefill-size` is divided by the attention-DP
+  size, so 16384 gives 4096 tokens per rank; keep that per-rank chunk at or below
+  `--max-prefill-tokens`. With `--tp 8 --attn-dp-size 8` on 72 GB
+  GPUs, lower `--mem-fraction-static` to 0.70 to leave room for the kernel.
+- The PD pairing validated so far is a decode server with
+  `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 --disaggregation-mode decode
+  --disaggregation-transfer-backend nixl` behind `sglang_router.launch_router --pd-disaggregation`,
+  with NIXL's UCX backend over RoCE (UCX device settings are site-specific).
+- Static expert placement (`--init-expert-location`, `--ep-num-redundant-experts`,
+  `--ep-dispatch-algorithm static`) is supported; `--enable-eplb` is not, and
+  speculative decoding is not validated (it needs an explicit
+  `--speculative-moe-runner-backend`).
+- `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_MEGAMOE_SM120_TRANSPORT_TABLE` picks the peer transport
+  (default `lsa_where_reachable`: PCIe/NVLink peer access where available, NCCL GIN
+  elsewhere).
+

+def _ue8m0_exponent_bytes(scale: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """UE8M0 exponent bytes of block scales stored as float32 powers of two."""
+    if scale.dtype == torch.float8_e8m0fnu:
+        return scale.view(torch.uint8)
+    exponents = scale.to(torch.float8_e8m0fnu)
+    if not torch.equal(exponents.to(scale.dtype), scale):
+        raise ValueError(
+            "FlashInfer SM120 MegaMOE requires power-of-two (UE8M0) FP4 block scales."
+        )
+    return exponents.view(torch.uint8)

+        MoEWeightPack(

+            w2=w2,
+            w13_scale=_ue8m0_exponent_bytes(layer.w13_weight_scale_inv.data),
+            w2_scale=_ue8m0_exponent_bytes(layer.w2_weight_scale_inv.data),

+        hidden_size=layer.hidden_size,

+    w13.copy_(transformed.w1_fp4)
+    copy_or_rebind_param(layer, "w13_weight_scale_inv", transformed.w1_sfb)
+    copy_or_rebind_param(layer, "w2_weight_scale_inv", transformed.w2_sfb)
+    layer._flashinfer_megamoe_cake_weights = dataclasses.replace(
+        transformed,
+        w1_fp4=w13,
+        w2_fp4=w2,
+        w1_sfb=layer.w13_weight_scale_inv.data,
+        w2_sfb=layer.w2_weight_scale_inv.data,
+    )

issue_comments.body:
@Fridge003 Thanks, rebased and resolved the conflicts.

The branch is now based on main (16eb87c); the conflict with #44036 (W4A16/SiTU) in flashinfer_megamoe.py has been resolved.

While re-validating on GPU, I hit a regression from #43607: the V4 decoder unconditionally passes leave_output_sum=True, but flashinfer_megamoe completes the EP combine inside its kernel and its FFN transport declares no sum group. The normal MoE path therefore returns MoEOutput pieces that the transport rejects during warmup with “transport finalize owes an undeclared sum group”.

The fix (bda748bc06) disables leave_output_sum specifically for flashinfer_megamoe, preserving other backends’ existing behavior. Tests exercise the real decoder and transport finalization, including a DeepGEMM fallback control. That fallback has a separate unresolved reduction-ownership issue and is not fixed here. The FlashInfer regression likely affects SM100 too; I could only verify it on SM120.

Btw, FlashInfer 0.7.2 does not include flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6346 yet, so the SM120 path remains an opt-in source install, with an explicit startup error under the default pin.
